name: Reclaimed Hall
desc: A derelict hall that the forest has already won — birch saplings stand in ranks out of a rubble-and-moss floor where the roof has fallen in, ivy comes down the window reveals and off the broken deck, plaster has mapped its way off the walls, and dust turns slowly in the light while every canopy sways on its own gust; cold urbex north light, high summer, a frozen winter, pure chiaroscuro, or a misregistered CMYK halftone.

energy.doc: how hard the light works — the wash from the roof hole, pool shimmer, dust brightness and contrast

scale.doc: how big the saplings and the roof failure are against the hall (rebuilds the room)

density.doc: how many saplings per rank, windows, ivy strands and dust motes

growth.doc: how far the forest has got — 0 is a bare shell, 1 is a hall full of trees and ivy

decay.doc: how far gone the building is — plaster loss, broken panes, rubble and how wide the roof has opened

hue.doc: palette hue shift off the default muted green / cold concrete

x.doc: where the roof has fallen in, and so where the light comes down

y.doc: the floor line at the back wall — how much frame is hall versus floor

style.doc: aesthetic: birch = pale saplings in dead concrete under cold north light, urbex large-format; verdant = high summer, heavy ivy, gold light, the hall has lost; frost = winter, bare stems, snow blown through the roof, blue-white and silent; chiaroscuro = no local colour at all, every form emerges purely from the light falloff; halftone = a misregistered CMYK four-plate print, rosette screens, no continuous tone

act.doc: multi-minute programme — a still summer, a gale working the canopies, or the light dying

seed.doc: regenerates the plaster loss, the sapling field, the ivy and the roof failure

alpha.doc: how far the world sits back behind the performers
